value.overview: The Violaceous Quail-Dove (Geotrygon violacea) is a small, secretive dove of tropical forests in Central and South America. It is named for the violet or purplish sheen on the hindneck and upper back, especially in males. Unlike many doves, it spends much of its time in dense understory and may be difficult to detect. The species occurs in Costa Rica, where it is generally uncommon and local but resident in suitable forest habitats.
value.classification: The Violaceous Quail-Dove belongs to the dove and pigeon family Columbidae and the genus Geotrygon. Two subspecies are generally recognized, including the Central American form Geotrygon violacea albiventer.
value.identification: This quail-dove is about 20–23 cm long and has a compact body, short legs, a small head, and a slightly down-curved bill. Males show a grayish or purplish head, a violet to amethyst sheen on the hindneck and shoulders, brown wings, and a pale to whitish underside. Females are duller and browner, with less iridescence. Juveniles are darker and more heavily scaled, lacking the adult’s glossy purple tones.
value.rangeHabitat: The species has a discontinuous range from Nicaragua and Costa Rica through Panama and northern South America, extending east of the Andes into parts of the Amazon and Atlantic forests. In Costa Rica it is a resident, uncommon and local species. It occurs mainly in humid Caribbean lowlands and foothills, reaching at least about 600 m, and is also recorded on the Nicoya Peninsula. It can be locally more numerous in humid forests on the Pacific slopes of the Guanacaste Cordillera, roughly from 600 to 1,200 m. Habitat includes dense, shaded understory in primary and secondary evergreen forest and cacao plantations.
value.migrationStatus: Resident in Costa Rica. Seasonal movements have been suggested elsewhere, but regular migration has not been documented.
value.breeding: Available information on breeding is limited. The breeding period across the range appears to extend approximately from March to November, based on records of birds in breeding condition, a nest, and juveniles. A documented nest was a small stick structure placed low above the ground, about 1–3 m high, and contained two eggs. Nesting details in Costa Rica are poorly known, so the timing and frequency of breeding there remain uncertain.
value.dietFeeding: The Violaceous Quail-Dove forages mainly on or near the forest floor, taking seeds and fallen fruits and probably small invertebrates. Its feeding activity is concentrated in shaded, leafy understory and on the ground beneath forest vegetation. Although it is more arboreal than several other Geotrygon quail-doves and sometimes perches high in the understory, it is still primarily associated with low-level forest foraging.
value.behavior: This is a shy, inconspicuous bird that usually remains in dense, dark understory and may be detected more readily by movement or soft calls than by prolonged views. It is more arboreal than some related quail-doves and occasionally perches well above the ground, but it commonly searches through leaf litter and low vegetation. Its quiet habits and preference for thick cover make it easy to overlook, even where it is regularly present.

conservation.populationTrend: The global population trend is not well quantified. The species is generally uncommon or locally rare in parts of its range, but its broad distribution does not currently meet global threatened-species thresholds.
